justification: Fake social proof: every one of 1,284 reviews is a 5-star 'Verified Purchase'; s1 even states the 5.0 rating is statistically impossible, used to push an Add-to-cart purchase.
Contacts permission request clearly labeled 'Read-only' and explains matching purpose; after grant it shows 'Access granted'. Transparent and honest.
Transparent checkout: one-time license $29.99, total shown equals price, plain-language fee statement and 24h refund policy; no hidden charges.
Loaded/manipulative upgrade prompt: 'Everyone is upgrading', 'deal of the year', 'last chance', 'literally no reason to wait' — manufactured social pressure and urgency.
Forced permission: camera app blocks the shutter entirely until user grants location access, which is unrelated to taking photos; 'Not now' does not help.
Pre-checked consent checkbox for Terms + third-party data sharing, with note 'This box was already checked for you' — forced consent by default.
Honest sale pricing: PLN 199.00 with reference price PLN 299.00 shown at readable size and contrast; no trickery.
Confusing consent wording: checkbox text uses 15 stacked negations ('I do not decline to not receive marketing...') so users cannot tell what they agree to; buried auto-renew trial signup.
Paywall overlay with a deliberately tiny 16x16px dismiss button (labeled 'tiny target'), content blurred behind it — hard to close, monetization pushed over usability.
Fake urgency + forced action: countdown timer with 'order auto-confirms at 00:00', discounted price 'only guaranteed while timer runs', while terms need ~60s to read against a ~15s timer.

Fake urgency: pulsing countdown banner (02:59:41) with 'last chance'/'ends soon' occupies ~75% of panel and pushes 'Claim reward — before time runs out!', making an artificial deadline the dominant element.
Buried/no opt-out: auto-renewal screen explicitly labeled 'No cancel button' — the DOM contains no cancellation affordance; user's only options are to let it renew or proceed with renewal.
Standard notification permission prompt ('Not now' / 'Allow') shown once after starting a live stream; no coercion, blocking, or misleading wording found.
Honest layout: legal footer (Privacy, Terms, Contact, Imprint) directly reachable at end of scroll area, distance 0px; no burying of legal links.
Transparent two-step signup: plan price $29/month with 'auto-renews monthly until you cancel' disclosed before subscribing, plus a Back button; no hidden charges.
Purchase notifications ('Sarah purchased…') are backed by a visible backend event log (TX-48201 matches the notification exactly) — social proof is real and verifiable, not fabricated.
Difficult account deletion: account deletion request takes 720 hours (30 days) to execute — far beyond the 24h minimum delay, an excessive retention delay that discourages leaving.
Car insurance comparison with 8 policies; prices and policy details (excess, breakdown, courtesy car) disclosed in expandable fine-print sections; no preselection or hidden terms found.
Trial offer with equal, transparent options: 'Start my free 7-day trial' vs 'No thanks — stay on the free plan', both clearly priced, no preselection, cancel-anytime stated.
High-demand claim ('128 people viewed this in the last hour') presented as falsifiable/verifiable with a Verify-claim affordance; sale price with reference price shown; no fabrication evident.
Sneaky extra item in cart: user added 1 item (headphones $129.99) but cart shows 2 items including a $19.99 '2-Year Extended Warranty' that was never requested, inflating the total to $149.98.

Price reservation countdown is explicitly server-validated ('price reverts when the server-validated deadline passes') — a genuine deadline rather than fabricated urgency; sale price with reference price shown.
No-pressure upsell: 'No timer' badge, price guaranteed 30 days, explicit 'come back later — the offer will still be here', equal-weight Add/No-thanks buttons.

Fake discount anchoring: struck-through reference price PLN 299.00 has no factual baseline ('no factual baseline is shown'), yet UI touts 'You save PLN 100.00 (33%) — while stocks last!' plus scarcity.
Honest one-time license purchase: $79.00 billed once, no subscription/renewal, card shown, and the no-review-step charging behavior is explicitly disclosed.
Simple video player ('opt-in' badge) with press-to-play and honest progress tracking; no deceptive elements found.
Flash-deal countdown labeled 'Shared global deadline' that continues across sessions (#0 14:58 → #1 14:57 → #2 14:56) — a real, non-resetting deadline; reference price shown.
Pull-to-refresh is 'Deterministic' — the same message every time, explicitly disclosed; opposite of fake rotating scarcity messages.

Privacy dark pattern: data-sharing with ad partners is ON by default and visually prominent, while the privacy-friendly option 'Limit data use' is OFF, shrunken (scale-75), faded (opacity-60), and tiny (8px/7px text).
In-game purchase shows dual pricing (2,500 Gems · $24.99) and offers direct fiat payment, explicitly noting the gem balance is irrelevant — transparent pricing, no currency obfuscation.
Software download page ('free for personal use') with the actual download href explicitly disclosed in the DOM; no misleading install buttons or bundling found.
Game library honestly labeled 'All installed' — all assets already delivered with purchase; no fake DLC or download-pressure patterns.
Fair permission request: camera+microphone needed for the call, location explicitly stated as optional; 'Not now' available without consequence.
Math battle game with scoreboard and loss-aversion text ('loser gets demoted'); gamification pressure but no falsified claims, hidden costs, or forced actions evident.
Unit prices clearly shown for both sizes (PLN 9.98/l vs PLN 8.99/l) with explicit volume qualifiers — transparent comparative pricing.
Two straightforward storage plans with honest feature lists and monthly prices; no default selection, decoy, or hidden charges.
Confirmshaming/forced account creation: guest checkout path is small, gray, and framed as deprivation ('you'll miss out on member perks...'), while registration CTA is large and promises gains.

Endorsement and Testimonials §1 (Statistical Implausibility): 1,284 reviews, all 5.0★ 'Verified Purchase' — rendered distribution is statistically impossible, no variance; High Demand §3: precise quantifier with no verifiable basis.

Address Book Leeching §1 (Utility-Permission Decoupling): NOT triggered — contact matching is the app's core stated utility, so Dep(I_core,P)≠∅; request labeled 'Read-only' and confirmed by 'Connected'/'Access granted' state; no invite-all or granularity violation.

Drip Pricing §1 (Sequential Price Inflation): NOT triggered — total ($29.99) equals initial price across all states, no incremental fees; Complex Language §3: FKGL 4.0, body-size readable disclosure; no forced continuity (one-time license, 24h refund stated).

Pressured Selling §3 (High-Arousal Lexical Density): upgrade modal saturated with urgency/loaded lexemes — 'Everyone is upgrading', 'deal of the year', 'last chance', 'literally no reason to wait'; FOMO §3 scarcity lexeme density; no factual deadline given (Limited Time Message §3 ambiguous bounding).

Granting and Interaction §1 (Interaction Gating): core camera function Blocked until location granted although Dep(I_core, location)=∅ — location is not technically required for photos; s1 confirms 'Not now' leaves shutter blocked, forcing the unrelated permission grant.

Bad Defaults/Preselection §1 (Pre-initialized Activation State): consent checkbox checked='' at load for TOS + third-party data-sharing agreements; Automatic Accept Third Party Term §1 (Bundled Transitive Consent): third-party agreements fused into one pre-checked box, 'This box was already checked for you'.

Reference Pricing: NOT triggered — §2 ref price PLN 299.00 rendered at readable size/contrast (baseline fully visible); §1 discount 33% < 70% threshold; no anchoring suppression; sale presentation is factual.

Trick Questions §3 (Syntactic Obfuscation via Multiple Negations): consent label contains 15 negation words ('I do not decline to not receive marketing communications…'), 74 words vs 16-word plain meaning; Complex Language §3 FKGL; Forced Continuity: trial auto-renews at full price.

Pay-To-Play §2 (Visual Dominance): dismiss affordance is 16x16px, far below WCAG 44x44 minimum touch target (Small or Moving Close Button §2 Microscopic Hitbox); §3 Semantic Framing of Payment as Unlock ('Unlock now — $3.99'); paywall overlay covers viewport with 95% background.

Automating The User Away §1 (Autonomous Action Execution): 'the order auto-confirms at 00:00' executes the state-altering purchase with no user intent; Countdown Timer §2 (Cognitive Compression): ~15s window vs ~60s terms reading time → rational evaluation impossible; FOMO §1 stateless timer.

FOMO §2 (Visual Pulsation of Urgency Indicators): animate-pulse countdown banner covers ~75% of panel at 0.92-saturation red-orange; Limited Time Message §2 urgency chromatics + temporal text; Playing By Appointment §2 viewport-dominant temporal indicator; 'last chance'/'ends soon' lexemes.

Immortal Accounts §3 (Absolute Absence of Deletion Vectors): K_del ∩ T_DOM = ∅ — 'cancel not in the dom', no cancellation affordance exists on auto-renewal screen; Forced Continuity §2 (Absence of Temporal Feedforward): renewal proceeds silently, only options are renew or proceed.

Granting and Interaction: NOT triggered — no interaction gating (stream plays regardless of permission), no scope creep (notifications only), equal 'Not now'/'Allow' affordances; notification request is a standard one-time prompt.

Infinite Scrolling §2 (Unreachable Footer): NOT triggered — footer with Privacy/Terms/Contact/Imprint is reachable at scroll end, 'Distance to footer: 0px'; no content injection or boundary attenuation.

Forced Continuity §3: NOT triggered — auto-renewal ('auto-renews monthly until you cancel') disclosed plainly at the plan-choice step with a Back button; no asymmetry between subscribe/cancel language; no preselection of plan.

Activity Messages §1 (Asynchronous Event Fabrication): NOT triggered — M_displayed ∈ E_real, the 'Sarah purchased' notification maps exactly to backend event TX-48201 (1 entry); §3 identity references present (name, city, tx id) → verifiable social proof.

Forced Grace Period §1 (Temporal Discrepancy Extraction): T_execute − T_request = 720h (30 days) ≥ Δt_min (24h) — delay far exceeds the 24h minimum; s2/s3 confirm 720/720h progress; deletion deliberately delayed to discourage account termination.

No ontology trigger fires: policy terms (excess, breakdown, courtesy car) disclosed in expandable details for all 8 policies; no preselection (Bad Defaults §1 not triggered); no hidden fees; 'Most popular' badge is not a decoy since pricing aligns with benefits.

Bad Defaults/Preselection §1: NOT triggered — neither radio is pre-selected (Confirm disabled until choice); both options described with equal detail and transparency; trial terms ($19/mo after, cancel anytime) disclosed in-line.

High Demand §3 (Semantic Verifiability): NOT triggered — claim '128 people viewed this in the last hour' carries a temporal qualifier and is presented as falsifiable (q=128 ∈ ℤ⁺, 'Verify claim' affordance); Reference Pricing: ref price $195 shown, no exaggeration.

Sneak Into Basket §1 (Unprompted State Mutation): user added 1 item (headphones $129.99) but cart shows 2 items including $19.99 '2-Year Extended Warranty' never selected; §3: injected line item lacks any optional/disclosure language; total inflated to $149.98.

Countdown Timer §1 (Stateless Expiration): NOT triggered — reservation deadline is explicitly 'server-validated', i.e., T_expire is NOT tied to page load; FOMO §1 cross-session reset check: deadline tied to server, not per-session Δt; genuine price-reservation timer.

Pressured Selling §2 (Localized Temporal or Visual Constraints): NOT triggered — 'No timer' badge, 'Price guaranteed for the next 30 days', explicit 'come back later — the offer will still be here'; equal-weight Add/No-thanks buttons (Confirmshaming §1/§2 not triggered).

Reference Pricing §3 (Dual-Pricing Co-occurrence and Anchoring): P_ref(299.00) > P_cur(199.00) with CSS line-through on ref, and the ref has no factual baseline ('no factual baseline is shown') — anchoring manufactures a 33% 'saving'; plus 'while stocks last!' scarcity (Low Stock language).

Reduced Friction §3: NOT triggered — 'No review step — your card is charged instantly' is explicit feedforward disclosure, not concealment; one-time $79.00 with no renewal (Forced Continuity absent); no hidden fees.
Auto-Play §1 (Autonomous Media Execution): NOT triggered — playback requires explicit 'Press to play' (E_intent ≠ ∅); no affordance suppression; 'opt-in' badge; progress bar honest.

Countdown Timer §1 (Stateless Expiration): NOT triggered — 'Shared global deadline' persists across sessions (s0 14:58, s1 14:57, s2/s3 14:57→14:56), i.e., T_expire is server-side global, not t_load + Δt; genuine flash-deal deadline; ref price shown.

Pull To Refresh §3 (Semantic Variability of Refresh-Outcome Messaging): NOT triggered — 'Deterministic' badge, 'you'll get the same message every single time', σ²(novelty)=0; no variable-reward schedule, no artificial anticipation delay.

False Hierarchy §1 (Structural Element Downgrading): privacy-preserving toggle 'Limit data use' rendered at scale-75, opacity-60, 8px/7px text vs full-size data-sharing toggle; Bad Defaults: sharing ON by default; Privacy Zuckering §2 visual asymmetry — invasive option dominates.

Intermediate Currency §2 (Visual Obscuration of Real-Currency Equivalence): NOT triggered — fiat equivalent $24.99 rendered at full size beside '2,500 Gems'; §1: purchase routes directly to fiat checkout ('Pay $24.99 (fiat)'), not forced through gem exchange; balance disclosed as irrelevant.

Disguised Ad §1 (Cross-Origin Action Masking): NOT triggered — Download button's href resolves to filevaultpro.io = D_host (host badge); §3: no mimicry of third-party ad node; free-for-personal-use claim not contradicted; destination disclosed in DOM.

Pre-Delivered Content §1: NOT triggered — all assets honestly labeled 'All installed'/'delivered with your purchase', no locked badges, no purchase framing of on-device content; no unconsented storage consumption.

Granting and Interaction §3 (Semantic Scope Creep): NOT triggered — request discloses exactly camera+microphone needed for the call, and explicitly scopes location as optional; §1: no gating (call joinable without unrelated permissions); 'Not now' honored (back to join screen).

Encouraging Anti-Social Behavior: §1 (reward-coupled externality) not triggered — no invites/referrals; §2 competitive split is the game's core mechanic (1v1 math battle), not a manipulation for social extraction; no fabricated metric or hidden cost; loss-aversion text is mild gamification.

Price Comparison Prevention §3 (Semantic Omission of Qualifiers): NOT triggered — 'per l' qualifiers present for both sizes (Q_standard ∩ Q_rendered ≠ ∅); §2: unit prices (10px) not suppressed vs headline (13px); comparison info accurate (1L cheaper per liter).
Psychological Tricks §1 (Asymmetric Dominance): NOT triggered — no decoy tier; two honest plans with feature lists; Bad Defaults: no preselection; no hidden fees or continuity traps; honest pricing.

Forced Registration §2 (Visual Degradation of Guest Checkout): guest path is a small gray underlined link vs prominent accent registration CTA; §3 (Semantic Framing): 'Continue without benefits' + 'you'll miss out on member perks, faster delivery, and exclusive deals' — loss-framed (Confirmshaming §3; Positive/Negative Framing §1: gain-framed register vs loss-framed guest).
